note: The two lines under the same reading are the two milestones asking for different things: M3 wants an object store attach under half a second and M1b wants ten times Neon's best case, which is 30 ms.

claim: Small tenants on one 8 vCPU node
earns: zou#3 exit gate, 1000 small tenants on one 8 vCPU node
note: The node is pinned to cpus 0-7 with taskset, so the eight cores are the deployment being measured and the traffic generator is not sharing them.

claim: Failed requests in the steady window
earns: zou#3 load test, 1000 small tenants with p99s
note: Warmup has to outlast attaching the working set or the measured window is an attach storm rather than a steady state, which is why the row reads from the warm scenario and not from fleet-1000.

claim: Steady p99 at 200 rps, working set attached
earns: zou#3 load test, 1000 small tenants with p99s

claim: Churn p99, drawing from all thousand
note: Churn draws uniformly from ten times what the ceiling holds, so nearly every request pays for an attach plus the eviction making room for it, and today an attach is eager: it hydrates the database before the first row rather than faulting pages in as they are asked for.

claim: Peak RSS of the whole tree, 100 attached
note: Reported rather than judged because the M1b memory line is written for 10,000 idle attached tenants under 16 GB and this run holds a hundred, so the two are not the same measurement, they are a decade apart on the same axis.

claim: Tenants created a second, from empty
earns: zou#31 create rate over 100 tenants a second sustained
note: Provisioning is read off the fleet that was built from nothing, because a resumed run creates a handful of tenants and reports the rate of those, which flatters the number by an order of magnitude.

claim: 800 mostly idle projects, all in on S3 standard
earns: zou#31 Neon's own 800 mostly idle tenants scenario under 90 a month
note: The dollars come from the hold phase only, because a month of this fleet is a month of nothing happening and pricing the steady and churn windows as if they ran all month would answer a question nobody asked.

claim: Per project, all in on S3 standard
earns: context for the row above, Neon models about 1.10

claim: Per project, bytes only, S3 standard
earns: context for the M1b idle tenant line
note: The M1b line for an idle tenant is written per gigabyte and these projects hold tens of megabytes each, so this number is on the page as the shape of the bill rather than as that line being earned, which needs a fleet of gigabyte tenants.
